title: Tool-return schema fallback & compatibility runbook + test suite
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem statement:
Customers are increasingly using function/tool-calling alongside our streaming JSON mode. When a tool returns structured payloads that conflict with the model's constrained-decoder expectations (extra fields, missing required keys, enum drift), behavior is inconsistent: sometimes the decoder rejects the combined stream, sometimes the model overwrites tool outputs, and sometimes downstream consumers receive invalid JSON.

Goal:
Establish a deterministic, tested fallback and reconciliation strategy so that tool-returned JSON is treated as authoritative when explicitly marked, model-produced tokens are validated against the active schema, and any discrepancies follow a documented transformation or rejection path. Deliver a runbook for operators and an automated test-suite that exercises edge cases across streaming, truncated tool outputs, and mixed-origin messages.

Scope:
- Decoder behavior when tool outputs precede/interrupt model streams in streaming mode.
- Fallback mapping rules for extra/unknown keys and enum mismatches.
- Validation policy permutations: strict (reject on mismatch), tolerant (strip unknowns), reconcile (attempt auto-coercion), and preserve-tool (tool wins).
- Observability hooks (metrics and traces) for schema violations and reconciliation decisions.
- E2E test harness that simulates function-calling flows, truncated responses, and load with batching enabled.

Out of scope (for this ticket):
- New SDK ergonomics (will be handled in a follow-up), on-prem install automation.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic compatibility policy matrix exists and is checked into docs/confluence with examples for each policy
Decoder unit tests cover: extra keys, missing required keys, enum drift, type coercion, and truncated tool payload mid-stream
E2E harness reproduces at least three real-world failure modes and asserts final JSON validity for each policy
Metric emission defined for: schema_violation.count, reconciliation.action (enum), tool_override.count
Canary rollout via console flag that toggles default policy to 'preserve-tool' without requiring runtime restarts
test_plan: Unit: Constrained-decoder tests simulate function-returned JSON objects and model fragments; assert deterministic decision per policy
Integration: End-to-end streaming test with tool-calling enabled; include delayed KV cache warmup and mid-response tool insertion
Chaos: Inject truncated tool payloads and random extra keys; verify reconciliation does not create invalid JSON in stream
Compatibility: Run against models A, B, and C (open variants + quantized) to validate kernel-level buffering doesn't reorder tool segments
Load: Run 1000 short requests/sec with batching to ensure reconciliation path scales and metrics are emitted without high CPU pressure
plan_steps: Design: Draft compatibility matrix and reconciliation rules (strict, tolerant, reconcile, preserve-tool)
Prototype: Implement a shim in the streaming decoder that tags tool-origin segments and applies policy-specific transforms
Tests: Add unit tests for tokenizer-level merged segments and parser-level JSON reassembly
Observability: Wire metrics + tracing spans for each reconciliation decision and add dashboard skeleton
Canary: Expose runtime flag via Console rollouts and run Canary against a subset of accounts
Docs/Runbook: Publish operator runbook with expected remediation steps for common violations
comments: 2026-03-02 - Aisha Kapoor: Kickoff notes: reached alignment with PM on 'preserve-tool' as default canary policy. Need clarity on data-masking for sensitive fields returned by tools.
2026-03-05 - Brent Morales: Implemented decoder shim prototype in draft branch 'feature/tool-preserve-shim'. Early unit tests pass for extra-key stripping behavior.

2026-03-08 - Priya Nair (QA): Found failure when tool payload contains nested arrays with nulls; added reproduction in CI harness. Recommending an additional coercion rule for null -> default-value in 'reconcile' policy.
2026-03-10 - Security: Reviewed and requested that tool-origin override must be auditable; adding 'tool_override' trace tag and immutable audit log entry. Marked ticket for security sign-off.
2026-03-13 - Brent Morales: Canary gate implemented; console flag 'structured_output.policy' added. Preparing rollout notes and dashboard panels for next week's canary
notes: Design decision: 'preserve-tool' should be opt-in per route until metrics show low violation rates
Trade-off: aggressive auto-coercion reduces immediate errors but may mask upstream model drift; prefer explicit reconciliation rules over heuristic fixes
Follow-up: PM to scope SDK ergonomics to expose policy selection in SDKs and server-side defaults
